subject.title: fix(sandbox): pipe docker exec command via stdin to prevent shell injection

question: Should Docker sandbox exec remain a shell-command surface, or should maintainers sponsor a compatibility-sensitive no-shell/validated-command mode to restrict metacharacters?
rationale: The submitted patch claims to stop shell syntax interpretation, but the current exec tool is a shell-command surface and piping to `/bin/sh` stdin does not change shell parsing; a true restriction would alter user-visible command semantics.

options.title: Preserve shell semantics and repair narrowly
options.body: Require the PR to fix the supervisor input wiring, remove the false metacharacter guarantee, and prove the real Docker behavior before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Sponsor a no-shell execution design
options.body: Treat the security goal as a larger product/security change with an argv or validated-command contract and compatibility proof.

options.title: Pause or close this approach
options.body: Close or replace this PR if the intended security property cannot be delivered without a broader contract change.

recommendation.title: Preserve shell semantics and repair narrowly
recommendation.body: Require the PR to fix the supervisor input wiring, remove the false metacharacter guarantee, and prove the real Docker behavior before reconsidering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has recent exec/sandbox-area history and is the best available routing owner for a security-sensitive command-contract decision.
